direction_summaries.explanation:
1. Detects the phrase “shift work” in clinical/epidemiological study contexts, i.e. occupational-exposure discussion in medical research.  
2. Picks up the heading “Thoughts” as a blog or personal-reflection section title in a web UI.  
3. Fires on “Chris <Surname>” constructions referring to sports figures in news headlines or articles.  
4. Activates on “Matt” when used as the given name of a high-profile media personality.  
5. Marks sentence-initial “Hope” whether used as a friendly opener (“Hope you…”) or as the abstract noun in academic prose.  
6. Flags the UI label “Related Posts” in online articles as a content-recommendation heading.  
7. Responds to the imperative “Talk about…” in headings or calls-to-action within reviews or guides.  
8. Highlights “Jonathan” when used as an author byline or personal name in announcements.  
9. Picks up passive-voice headline patterns like “Evidence sought” in news stories.  
10. Detects the proper name “Jayamala,” i.e. Indian public-figure references.  
11. Marks narrative openings starting with “Ever since…” in both informal and promotional copy.  
12. Activates on two-word technical medical terms beginning with “psych… morbidity.”  
13. Fires on “Gary” when used as a first name in informal diagnostic or troubleshooting dialogue.  
14. Picks up the verb “urges” in news reporting, signaling public advisories or calls for action.

In effect, it flags the punctuation that separates or closes off a modifier or clause.
